Definition: Cush (or Ethiopia), the name of a son of Ham, and of his territory; also of an Israelite
BiblicalUsage: Cush is the son of Ham and the father of peoples, and the name covers a man, a people, and a land. Genesis 10:6 lists Cush among the sons of Ham, the title of Psalms 7 names "Cush the Benjamite" — a different Cush, an Israelite whose words against David drew the psalm — and Isaiah 18:1 speaks of the land beyond the rivers of Ethiopia.
TheologicalSignificance: I am convinced this name's range is the point: from Ham's son to a Benjamite accuser to the far land of Ethiopia, the Bible keeps Cush in the story, and God keeps every nation in His sight.
